description: Granular audio processor, an expanded version of Clouds by Mutable Instruments, with its own knob, CV input and attenuverter for each of nine parameters

params.text: Selects the point in the recording buffer the grains are played from; turning clockwise travels back in time
Sets the length of each grain
Transposes the grains; at the centre the buffer plays at the pitch it was recorded at
At the centre no grains are generated; clockwise from there they are sown at random, counter-clockwise from there at a steady rate
Morphs the grain envelope from a rectangle through a triangle to a raised cosine, and past about two o'clock brings in a diffuser that smears transients
Steps the recording buffer through 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds, the sample rate falling as the time grows; the lamp for the chosen length blinks until the buffer is full
Stops new audio being written to the buffer, so the grains carry on playing from the material already there
Fires a single grain by hand
Steps through the four memory banks, loading the audio buffer stored in each
Silences the audio going into the buffer, and holds the red lamp of the input meter on
Silences the signal path ahead of the reverb, so reverb tails ring on rather than being cut off
Sets the level of the audio going into the buffer, reaching 6dB of gain fully clockwise, and sets the baseline that the input VCA voltage is added to
Sets how much of the processed output is written back into the buffer
Sets how widely the grains are scattered across the stereo field
Sets the balance between the dry input and the processed signal
Sets the amount of reverb on the output
Sets the final output level, reaching 6dB of gain fully clockwise, and sets the baseline that the output VCA voltage is added to
Attenuates and inverts the voltage reaching its parameter, from that parameter's own CV jack, from AUX, or from the internal random generator; at the centre no modulation gets through

inputs.text: A voltage added to the IN knob, changing the input level of both channels equally
A voltage added to the OUT knob, changing the output level of both channels equally
A gate here stops new audio being written to the buffer for as long as it is high
A pulse here fires a single grain
Transposes the grains exponentially, tracking one volt per octave, and is summed with the linear pitch CV
One voltage distributed to all nine parameters; a parameter whose own CV jack is patched takes that jack instead
The left audio input, which feeds both channels while the right input is empty
A voltage for that one parameter, scaled by that parameter's attenuverter, and it disconnects AUX and the internal random generator from that parameter

outputs.text: The left channel of the processed stereo output
The right channel of the processed stereo output

notes: the grains are played from a recording of whatever is patched to the audio inputs, so nothing comes out of the module until audio is patched in
with DENSITY at its centre no grains are generated at all, so the module passes the dry signal and nothing else
the recording buffer has to fill before the grains have material to play; the lamp for the chosen TIME length blinks until it has
menu: Alternate mode — chooses Granular, Pitch-shifter/time-stretcher, Looping delay, Spectral madness, Oliverb, Resonestor, Beat repeat or Spectral clouds
Save buffer — writes the current contents of the recording buffer into one of the four banks, listed as Bank A to Bank D
Normalize AUX to random CV — switches the internal stepped 0-5V random generator on and off; while it is on and AUX is empty it reaches every parameter whose own CV jack is empty
Set random CV frequency from PAN knob — reads the PAN knob to set how fast the internal random voltage steps, 1Hz fully counter-clockwise and 100Hz fully clockwise

inputs.4: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
